- When sentiment is low (≤0.18) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 2-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- Model frequently underestimates early in the 30-day horizon (e.g., days 1–5) when sentiment is neutral or negative; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 3 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.18–0.53), model exhibits lag; forecast should be adjusted to match recent 7-day average, not 30-day trend.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after spike), model often holds too high; apply 1–3% downward correction in next 3–7 days.
- For sentiment history with high variance (e.g., 0.09–0.53 alternating), model overfits short-term noise; use 5-day smoothing or sentiment-weighted average for correction.
